scope: Static shipped-client moderation contracts, distinct from preservation-server policy and dashboard authorization.

framing.indices: Zero-based response tokens after the existing HTTP response wrapper; TCP payload indices exclude its opcode token.
framing.escaping: These senders concatenate delimiter-separated fields without per-field escaping. The existing outer transport encrypts the complete payload.
framing.safety: Do not accept delimiter or line-break injection in authored reasons, badges, reports, or wire text. Encryption and client-supplied identifiers are not moderator authorization.

gates: Response nonce must equal the stored request nonce.
http.effects: Banned=true creates or updates BannedUntil and loads UserBanned; false invokes the continuation.
http.authority_limit: Persona name and hardware/network fields are client claims. Bind account policy to authenticated ingress authority, not these fields.

http.effects: Creates or updates BannedUntil from fields 5/6. Banned=true loads UserBanned. If not banned, an incorrect PS4ID echo causes Application.Quit; the existing-login branch continues through ChannelGUID.
http.identity_note: On the shipped Steam bootstrap, sAccountId is the Steam account identifier and PS4ID. Echo request field 3, not the persona-name field 0.
http.testing_note: isTesting is parsed only while its existing client value is false. isDev is a client-supplied boolean, not a permission grant.

http.effects: Banned=true loads UserBanned. Existing login and matching PS4ID continue through ChannelGUID; other branches select sign-in/terms. Unlike N2UserExist, identity mismatch does not directly call Quit.
The login continuation calls Application.Quit(0) when false. True starts online-time updates and the existing space-load path.
http.limit: This reply has no ban date/description or separate ban flag; false is admission failure, not proof of a particular sanction.

http.effects: Requires current GUID. Banned=true loads UserBanned. Not banned and noFreeSlot=true invokes the no-slot callback; otherwise begins HTTPSpaceLoading.
http.limit: No expiry or reason is parsed here; this path does not populate those display fields.

http.effects: After literal/GUID/account checks, target must resolve to a current Memory player. JSON hydrates name/status/mood/color. When present, response field 5 is copied verbatim to NebulaPlayer.staff at offset 0xD0; SetValues assigns lblStaff.text and the nickname color.
http.role_limit: No native role enum, accepted staff-value list, or moderation permission check was recovered in this path. A badge is display data, not authority; a preservation server must authorize actions independently.

request: report text; empty string becomes literal 0
http.effects: Requires current GUID echo. True shows the sent-report flow; false shows UserPreviouslyReported.
limits: The native request has a target username but no target platform/account field.
Receipt presentation does not prove historical storage, review, deduplication scope, or moderator workflow.

http.effects: Poll coroutine waits 10 seconds between sends. With matching GUID and a space/editor context, a nonzero value not previously displayed is shown in txtMinutes for 5 seconds, then hidden. Zero and repeated values are ignored until resetRemainingTimes.
http.limit: The value is displayed as an integer in a field named txtMinutes. It is not arbitrary announcement text or client-side shutdown enforcement.
This is a startup status gate, not a general message channel.

ban_screen.permanent_effect: The literal string null selects the built-in permanent-suspension text.
ban_screen.timed_effect: Other date strings replace the literal (x) in the existing date label. No DateTime/integer parse or expiry enforcement occurs here.
ban_screen.description_effect: Description is assigned directly to its Text component.
ban_screen.policy_limit: The backend must enforce expiry. A readable UTC expiry string is an authored formatting choice, not a recovered original server date convention.

personal_silence.effects: Refresh resolves username/platform to a current GUID and refetches relationship state. Space-chat receive drops a silenced remote. This is viewer-to-target relationship behavior, not source proof of an account-wide moderator mute.

current_scene_transport.behavior: Active Mirror client decrypts NebulaMessage and splits on #. Queue parses the first token as TypeTCP and calls only a registered processor, passing the remaining tokens as its payload.
chat_constraints: Space type 0 requires a non-null current Memory player even for Public. Unknown GUID lookup returns null; there is no SYSTEM exception in Memory.GetNebulaPlayer.
Nonzero chat types bypass some ordinary Space relationship filters; that does not define a new System/moderator enum or confer permission.
A SYSTEM formatting literal exists elsewhere, but does not bypass the Space processor's missing-player rejection.
current_scene_transport.notification_limit: No global-warning/moderator-announcement type is declared in this enum.
current_scene_transport.closing_effect: Reads payload index 1 as instance identifier, compares current instance, then performs existing redirect-to-Nexus behavior. This is an instance-close path, not proof of a targeted moderation-kick reason channel.

legacy_support_screen.display_effect: SupportScreen.Start assigns PS4Info.supportScreenMessage at offset 0x228 to its Text component.
legacy_support_screen.current_route_limit: No admitted network producer for that field was recovered on the current Mirror/ProcessorQueue path. TypeTCP 32 is Board_msg_InitGame; legacy 141 and 999 must not be treated as current support-screen/close commands without a separately reviewed receiver.

limitations: Static shipped-artifact evidence only; no game or server was launched for this analysis.
Original server persistence, expiry policy, staff-role semantics, moderation permissions and operational workflows are not established by client code.
The scene TypeTCP enum contains no separately named moderator ban, mute, kick or global-announcement command. This bounded finding does not prove that no historical out-of-band tooling existed.
Legacy transport constants, personal relationship controls, platform chat restrictions and developer flags must not be conflated with authenticated server moderation authority.

Some earlier decompiler exports lost branches after GC write barriers. Critical missing-player, permanent-ban and popup timing findings were checked against bounded raw instructions and metadata literals.
The backend/dashboard implementation and its capabilities must be documented and tested separately before claiming working operator moderation or native delivery.
